title: Dr. Nelson, Mrs. Nelson and other Napoleonville bands
summary: Bands in Napoleonville: Dr. Nelson's band, his wife the town's music teacher, Bill Smuthers and later Ernest Himes.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Yeah. Um, were there any bands in Napoleonville? How big, I don't, I've been through there on the bus but never did stop to see the town. Well, there was bands there. Um, Dr. Nelson had a band. That was a colored doctor. He has two sons here right now. There's Lewis Nelson and George Nelson. Oh, it's that doctor. I knew the Dr. Nelson. He just died, you know, a month or two ago. Well, that's Lewis Nelson's dad. And he was up there. He had a band there and his wife was the only music teacher in Napoleonville, Mrs. Nelson. Yeah, I guess his son told us about it. I forgot about it.
And by the way, the first job I ever played in my life, I played it with Lewis and George Nelson. That is in Napoleonville, because we both walked in the same town.
I know their mother was trained, I think, at the Boston Conservatory, Louis Nelson. Right. Miss Nelson had a band there. And I remember there was a trombone player, you'll call it,
Bill Smuthers. He had a band there at that time. Since then, Ernest Himes came from Napoleonville, from Donisonville, in organizing there. And he's still there. He's still there with his band.
